encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller. The banners of {my_faction} do not bow to strangers who carry such a scowl. State your business before my hearth-fire grows cold.
{player}, your name has been spoken at the crossroads with little honour. Let us see whether your deeds match the tales told of you.
Well met, ser {player}. The road is wide enough for two banners, though I would know your purpose before we part ways in the mud of this valley.
Ser {player}! By the warmth of my hearth at Dolmare, it gladdens me to see you on this road. Sit by the fire and tell me what news travels from the east.
Ah, {player}, a friend beneath an open sky. Let us walk together for a while and see whether our banners can share the same field of glory.

encounter_threatened.text: {gold} gold, you say? Ser {player}, I will not hand over a single coin to a demand barked at me on the open road. Draw your blade if you must.
Ser {player}, you name a price of {gold} gold and call it a toll. A toll is paid to a lord, not demanded at sword point. Speak again with courtesy and we may yet talk.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for I have heard your jests before. Yet even a jest with {gold} gold on its tongue must be answered. Let us settle it fairly, friend.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept your proposal, ser {player}. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the ancestors witness the oath we swear here today.
An alliance against {enemy_faction} suits my purpose well, ser {player}. Yet a pact is only as strong as the hands that hold it, so keep your word or lose your honour.
Gladly, ser {player}! Our oath is sworn and our swords are pledged against {enemy_faction}. I shall long remember what {rival} has owed us, and I will see that debt paid.

encounter_alliance_no.text: You offer me an alliance while {rival} still walks freely? Ser {player}, I will not sully my banner that way. Let the road remember this refusal.
No, ser {player}. An alliance born of a demand is no alliance at all. Go and find some other banner willing to be used, for mine will not be lent so cheaply.
I must decline, ser {player}. A banner that has sung for the fallen cannot lightly march beside {rival}. Consider this a matter of conscience, not a slight.
Forgive me, friend {player}, but I cannot take this oath at present. My honour is tied to matters I must settle first, and I trust you will understand when the road allows another meeting.

captured_by_player.text: So the wheel of fortune has turned against me, ser {player}. Take my sword and my shame, but I will not bow my head. Name your ransom, and {my_faction} will pay what honour demands.
Do not gloat, ser {player}. Every captive of {my_faction} has kin who sing their name at dusk, and I will not be the one who forgets. Take what you must and be done.
Well fought, ser {player}. The field went to your banner today and I am your captive by the rules of war. Let us speak plainly of terms, for I do not wish this to end in bitterness.
Ser {player}, I yield with a lighter heart than I expected, for I know you fight as a true knight should. Hold me under guard if you must, but treat me with the courtesy due a fallen banner.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you could have wrung gold from me yet chose mercy. My hearth at Dolmare is open to you.
Ser {player} gave me my freedom without a single coin asked. Such honour is rare on any road. Let the songs of Dolmare tell of it.
Ser {player}, you spared me the ransom today. I owe that mercy a debt, though I do not yet know how I will repay it.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A banner abandoned in the field is a sorrow that will be sung for long.
{player}, you turned from {my_faction} for {faction}. That wound will not close quickly. Go with what honour you still carry.
{player}, I hear you have joined {faction}. Every oath is yours to weigh, and I shall not judge you before the ancestors do.
{faction} now claims ser {player}, who once marched under {my_faction}. Let the songs remember the oaths sworn in both camps.

war_declared.text: The horns sound! {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}, and every fallen banner shall be sung for at Dolmare.
Hear me, travellers of Ormerath. {my_faction} takes up the sword against {enemy_faction}. May their ancestors bear witness to our cause.
Oaths have been broken and blood demands answer. {my_faction} now stands at war with {enemy_faction}. Let honour guide every blade.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, what a glorious field! With {troop_count} banners at our backs we shattered {enemy_faction}, and it was honour to fight beside you. Let our ancestors look down and see what we have wrought.
Ser {player}, we came through the press together and {enemy_faction} lies broken. Our {troop_count} banners held the line. I am content to have shared such a field with you.
Ser {player} and I broke {enemy_faction} today with {troop_count} banners beside us. Such a victory deserves a song.
{player}, your blade rang true with {troop_count} of us in the press. I will sing of that charge at my hearth. Thank you, friend.

encounter_farewell.text: We part for now, ser {player}, but our quarrel does not end with this parting. Let the road remember what was said between our banners.
Fare well, ser {player}. May your path be straight and your banners fly high. Should our roads cross again, we shall greet each other with honour.
The sun leans low and I must ride on, ser {player}. Keep your oaths true and your blade honest, and we will meet again beneath kinder skies.
Farewell, dear friend {player}. May the hearth of Dolmare welcome you whenever the road brings you near. Go with the blessing of your ancestors.

ambient_chatter.text: The mist lies heavy over {village} this morning. Such weather makes men sing of their fallen, and I am glad of the company.
Has anyone travelled from {town} lately? I bring news of a fine feast at Dolmare and a pledge to sing for every banner lost this season.
The roads between {town} and {village} are muddy, but honour does not wait for dry ground. Ride on, friends, and keep your banners high.
A wagon of wine passed {village} at dusk. I raised a toast to every fallen banner. Will any travellers raise a cup with me?
